On-Chain Operator. Lesson 11.1, Hedging price exposure with perps and options. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already know a health factor and a stop. A hedge is another written path. It is not a claim that the risk is gone.
Perp hedge: short a perpetual future against spot you hold.
Cheap to open; pays or earns funding; needs margin; the hedge ratio is your choice.
Protective put: buy the right to sell at a strike.
Costs a premium, and your loss is capped below the strike.
Collar: buy a put and sell a call to pay for it.
A hedge costs something (premium, funding, capped upside).
Hedge the risk you can't afford, not every risk.
Work the example on paper. You hold 10 ETH at $3,000 ($30,000). Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Work the example on paper. 50% perp hedge (short 5 ETH): ETH falls 30% → spot −$9,000, short +$4,500 → −$4,500 (−15%) instead of −30%. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Protective put: buy a 30-day $2,700 put for 2% ($60/ETH). Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Work the example on paper. Worst case per ETH = $300 drop to the strike + $60 premium = $360 (12%), however far ETH falls in that month. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Hedge target stated (which risk, how much). If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Cost computed (premium, funding, capped upside). If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Margin buffer for perp hedges set. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. What does a protective put cap? The answer: Your loss below the strike, for the option's term, at the cost of the premium.
Check yourself. 2. What does a collar trade away? The answer: Upside above the call strike, to pay for the put.
Check yourself. 3. 20 ETH, 25% perp hedge, ETH −40%. Net loss if ETH was $3,000? The answer: Spot −$24,000, short +$6,000 → −$18,000.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to reduce price exposure deliberately, and know what each hedge costs.
